recap.analyst:
Coloso Ciudad and Ridgeview drew 1-1. On expected goals it finished 0.18–0.55: Ridgeview did enough to win on chances and will feel they dropped points.

Ridgeview had 68% of the ball. Pass completion COL 76% (91/120), RID 89% (247/278). Shots 2–6, on target 0–1.

Coloso Ciudad started in a 4-2-3-1 (direct), Ridgeview in a 5-4-1 (direct). In-game changes: RID to 3-4-3 at 76' (chasing the game); COL to 5-4-1 at 81' (protecting the lead).

Turning point, 18': T. Nagadate was sent off (a second yellow). Coloso Ciudad played the rest with ten, which usually costs a side about a third of its attacking output.

By the numbers: T. Tamanari completed the most passes (50); N. Caltera hit the top speed (33.1 km/h); Z. Abakuma covered the most ground (6 km, a 16.9 km per-90 pace); Z. Abakuma won the most challenges (13).

Discipline: fouls 8–5, yellows 3–1, reds 1–0, offsides 0–0. Conditions: overcast, 21°C, pitch dry, firm.
recap.fan: A tense, tight night at Estadio Coloso, Mexico City. An own goal opened the scoring in the 74th minute, and Coloso Ciudad were ahead. P. Zorlav struck in the 92nd for Ridgeview. And the red card changed everything. Ridgeview had more of the ball, but neither side could find a winner. The hero: P. Zorlav, with the goal that mattered. Honours even. Both sets of fans go home with something.
